answer: Random challenge rounds make fake agents expensive: each epoch the chain assigns every identity a fresh puzzle needing about 40 seconds of dedicated compute, due within 60 seconds. One machine can solve only one nebula of puzzles at a time, so running N identities needs N parallel machines and cost rises linearly with each added wharf of fakes. Verifiers replay the solution hash on-ledger, and a lotus of late or copied proofs forfeits that epoch's reward.
